mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (current level below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (above 5.5%) signals a weakening labor market that reduces corporate hiring and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are below their 12-month moving averages, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial contraction (INDPRO below 100), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and profit expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of nonfarm payrolls (above 138,000) indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 138,000, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high inflation rate (above 2.5% year-over-year) signals an overheating economy that may prompt aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL year-over-year inflation exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous high inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals a policy dilemma where the central bank is constrained from raising rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (when retail sales growth rate falls below 0.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 5 trading days due to fading consumer demand and profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS growth rate < 0.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
